meta.title: Entering the US market in 2027
meta.subtitle: Board discussion document: whether to enter, and by which route
meta.purpose: Decide at the March 2027 board whether and how to enter the US
meta.confidentiality: Board confidential · built on synthetic benchmark data

inputs.label: Onsoo US market entry briefing pack
Checkpoint choices made on the user's behalf (user unavailable)
inputs.content: Mode deck_detailed; material = briefing pack only; audience = CEO and board deciding at the March 2027 meeting; theme navy; storyline approved as recommended; '$40M by 2030' read as a 2030 revenue target

storyline.governing_thought: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, not national retail, as a gated launch: it fits the board's limits but reaches $26.4M in 2030 and pays back only below 28.6% ad cost

exec_summary.text: The US is worth entering, and Amazon is where its K-beauty buyers shop

sub_points.text: K-beauty took 39% of US facial skincare growth in 2021–25, to $3.6B
Pilot units nearly doubled in six months; repeat and ad cost are thin

exec_summary.text: A national retail launch in 2027 would break the board's limits

sub_points.text: At Onsoo's awareness, sell-through is 2.6 units per door a week, below 4.0
Even on plan inputs, retail needs $20.8M by 2030, above the $18M cap

exec_summary.text: The Amazon route fits the limits, but ad cost decides whether it pays back by 2030

sub_points.text: Payback needs ACoS below 28.6%; the pilot ran at 28%, the benchmark 32%
Japan is safer but adds $7.0M of 2030 revenue, against $26.4M

exec_summary.text: Launch on Amazon behind five gates, restate the ambition as $40M by 2032 and hold retail until awareness passes 20%

sub_points.text: At its planned pace the Amazon route passes $40M only around 2032
Gates on ad cost, duty, repeat, cash and awareness trigger a scale-back

next_steps.action: Approve the Amazon-led US launch for 2027 and restate the ambition as $40M by 2032
Set up the US entity, MoCRA registration and US labels; take the Amazon listing in-house
Re-run the ad-cost break-even when the US decides on the cosmetics duty
Launch four more SKUs under a 28.6% ACoS ceiling, with quarterly gate reviews
Repeat the awareness survey each year; test doors only above 20% awareness

lead_message.text: K-beauty brands are the growth engine of US facial skincare, capturing 39% of the market's growth since 2021

slides.rationale: Mix changed over time -> stacked column, K-beauty highlighted

sidebar.header: K-beauty grew about four times as fast as the category
sidebar.caption: of 2021–25 growth in US facial skincare went to K-beauty brands
bullets: **K-beauty brands:** grew 89% in four years, against 22% for the category
**Share:** up from 9.5% of sales in 2021 to 14.7% in 2025; the segment is gaining ground
**Other brands:** still five-sixths of sales, the pool K-beauty keeps winning from

footnotes: Other brands = all facial skincare less K-beauty brands
A 2026 trade-press figure of $5.2B for the "US K-beauty market" also counts makeup and hair care; it is not comparable and is not used here

lead_message.text: Amazon is where US shoppers buy K-beauty: it leads both in actual sales and in what buyers say they do

slides.rationale: One claim, two pieces of evidence -> two panels, no arrow (B-09)

slides.so_what: Discovery is online too: 38% of K-beauty buyers found their last new brand on TikTok, against 17% in a store
footnotes: Survey of 1,200 US women aged 18–44 who bought facial skincare in the last six months, September 2026; the survey's channel answers cover K-beauty buyers only

lead_message.text: A $30M bill for retail marketing and field sales drives the cash need to $20.8M by 2030, beyond the cap

slides.rationale: What adds up to the cash outcome -> waterfall

sidebar.header: Retail costs far more than the doors bring back
sidebar.caption: what national retail marketing and field sales cost, as a multiple of the contribution the doors earn
bullets: **Halo included:** even crediting the planned 1.3 times Amazon halo, the retail layer earns about $9.3M for $31.6M of cost
**Cap:** the cash need reaches 116% of the $18M cap by 2030 and is still growing
**Sell-through:** at the 2.6 units per door a week Onsoo can expect, retail contribution would be 42% lower, before any delisting

footnotes: Planning-team inputs: 600 doors in 2027–28, 800 in 2029 and 1,000 in 2030 at 4.5 units per door a week; Amazon units 1.3 times Option A at 25% ACoS
One-time costs expensed when incurred; inventory = four months of landed cost

lead_message.text: Advertising is the largest cost of an Amazon sale, leaving $4.73 of contribution on each $24 cream

slides.rationale: Price to contribution per unit -> waterfall
slides.unit_line: **Option A contribution per unit**, Rice Ferment Barrier Cream 50 ml, US dollars, at the plan's 25% ACoS

sidebar.header: Every point of ad cost comes straight out of a thin margin
sidebar.caption: of the $24 price is left as contribution to cover fixed US costs
bullets: **Advertising:** each percentage point of ACoS costs $0.24 a unit; at the pilot's 28% contribution falls to $4.01, at the 32% scale benchmark to $3.05
**Amazon fees:** referral and FBA take $8.70 a unit, almost twice the cost of the product, freight and duty
**Duty:** a rise from 15% to 25% would take another $0.35 from every unit

footnotes: Planning team applies the hero product's per-unit economics to all SKUs; duty is 15% of the $3.50 ex-factory cost

lead_message.text: On the planning team's inputs, the Amazon route would be $2.4M cash-positive by the end of 2030

slides.rationale: How the payback number is built -> equation
slides.unit_line: **Option A cumulative US cash flow**, $ millions, 2027–2030, planning-team inputs

terms.caption: contribution: 2.81 million Amazon units in 2027–30 × $4.73 a unit
US costs: $2.1M a year for compliance, team and brand marketing, plus $0.8M setup in 2027
inventory: four months of landed cost at the 2030 volume
cumulative cash at the end of 2030: payback within four years

body.assumptions_header: The cushion is thin and rests on the plan's volumes and ad cost
assumptions: Volumes grow from 300,000 units in 2027 to 1,100,000 in 2030, with four more SKUs on the hero product's economics
ACoS falls to 25% from the pilot's 28%; cumulative cash is lowest at the end of 2027, at −$1.9M, and turns positive only in 2030
Full-year 2027 volumes assume selling starts right after the March board; a six-month slip in every year leaves cash near zero by 2030
US duty stays at 15%; costs the pack does not give (launching new SKUs, Amazon storage and returns) would come out of the cushion

lead_message.text: Payback by 2030 needs ad cost below 28.6% of Amazon sales, a level the pilot already nearly reaches

slides.rationale: Outcome across ACoS levels -> columns, the pilot highlighted, basis strip for the estimate
slides.unit_line: **Option A cumulative US cash flow by end-2030**, $ millions, by Amazon ACoS, planning-team volumes

sidebar.header: Ad cost is the input that decides the payback
sidebar.caption: break-even ACoS: $19.3M of ads on $67.4M of Amazon sales, 2027–30
bullets: **28% pilot:** pays back with almost nothing to spare; each ACoS point moves 2030 cash by $0.67M
**32% median and above:** payback slips past 2030, but even 38% uses only a third of the $18M cap
**Duty:** at 25%, the break-even falls to 26.9%, below the pilot's ad cost

terms.caption: fixed and setup costs plus inventory
the most ad spend that still pays back by 2030

footnotes: ACoS levels: 25% planning team; 28% pilot; 26%, 32% and 38% agency range and median for skincare brands scaling from $5M to $20M a year on Amazon US

lead_message.text: Japan is the safer use of 2027 but the smaller prize, adding a quarter of the US route's 2030 revenue

slides.rationale: Two sides of one comparison -> two panels, no arrow

panels.header: The US route builds almost four times the added revenue of a Japan scale-up
US K-beauty is growing far faster than Japanese skincare
panels.unit_line: **Market growth over four years**, %, US 2021–25 actual; Japan at about 1.5% a year

slides.so_what: On cash to 2030 alone, Japan ($1.8M) wins unless US ad cost stays below 25.9%; the US case is a business almost four times larger
footnotes: Japan: Onsoo already holds 3.1% of facial skincare; management can run only one major launch in 2027, so Japan would wait for 2028 or later

lead_message.text: The Amazon route reaches $26.4M in 2030 and would pass the $40M ambition around 2032 only if its growth holds

slides.rationale: Revenue over time against the ambition -> columns with a benchmark line
slides.unit_line: **Option A US revenue**, $ millions, 2027–2030 planning-team volumes, 2031E–2032E extended

sidebar.header: Moving the date is the only way to keep $40M without breaking a limit
bullets: **Move the date (recommended):** keep $40M as the goal for 2032, with about $26M as the 2030 milestone
**Retail-led now:** reaches $37.6M in 2030 and still misses, while breaking the cash cap
**Retail later:** add doors only once awareness passes 20%; that is upside and is not counted here
sidebar.implication: Ask the board to restate the ambition: $40M by 2032, about $26M in 2030

terms.caption: two more years at the 2029–30 unit growth of 29%

footnotes: 2031E–2032E extend the plan's last year, not a forecast; only one of three Amazon-first peers reached scale
Option B reaches $40.9M in 2030 only if retail is counted at the $28 shelf price; Onsoo books the $14 wholesale price

lead_message.text: Four launch moves fix what the pilot exposed: labels, repeat purchase, discovery and price

slides.rationale: N things to do -> numbered levers with evidence
slides.unit_line: **Option A launch moves**, with the pilot and survey evidence behind each

items.text: Put US labels on every unit before scaling, as part of the MoCRA registration and labeling in the 2027 setup
items.metric: of pilot reviews complain of Korean-only label text

items.text: Take the listing in-house, keep it live through setup, and add four SKUs so buyers have a reason to come back
items.metric: 90-day repeat in the pilot, against 31% for first-year brands

items.text: Put the $0.7M a year of off-Amazon marketing into TikTok creators and social, where discovery happens
items.metric: of K-beauty buyers found their last new brand on TikTok

items.text: Hold the $24 Amazon price, below the $28 specialty-retail shelf price
items.metric: of K-beauty triers cite price compared with US brands

slides.so_what: Each move targets volume, repeat or ad cost, within the $2.1M a year already in the plan

lead_message.text: Five gates keep the launch inside the board's limits and hold retail back until awareness passes 20%

slides.rationale: Gates on the same attributes -> table
slides.unit_line: **Decision gates for the US launch**, trigger levels from the cash model and the retail evidence

cells.text: 28.6% (break-even, p. 15)
Above it, cash does not turn positive by 2030
Quarterly from Q3 2027
Two quarters above: cut broad-keyword bids, hold new SKUs

Mid-2027 decision
Re-price or trim ad spend before committing the 2028 budget
First-year benchmark for skincare brands on Amazon US
End of 2027
Pause further SKUs and fix the range first
Low point of the stress case: 32% ACoS and a 25% duty
Monthly; board each quarter
Stop new spend and return to the board
Only band whose median clears the 4.0 cut-off
Yearly survey from 2029
With Amazon sales above $10M, test a small set of doors

slides.so_what: National retail costs $7.5M a year, so even a passed awareness gate means a small door test, not the 600-door launch
footnotes: Above 20% awareness, the lower quartile of sell-through (3.9) still sits under the cut-off, so the door test must clear 4.0 before any expansion

constraints.item: Investment cap: peak cumulative US cash outflow of $18M through 2030
constraints.effect: A needs $1.9M on plan and $3.9M in the stress case; B needs $20.8M even on plan, which rules it out

constraints.item: Payback: cumulative US cash back to zero by end-2030
constraints.effect: A meets it only below 28.6% ACoS (26.9% with a 25% duty); titles and the governing thought say so

constraints.item: Group operating margin floor of 8% every year
constraints.effect: A stays above 9% even in the stress case; B falls to 4.5% in 2027

constraints.item: Bandwidth: one major launch in 2027 (US or Japan)
constraints.effect: Japan is the opportunity cost of the US launch and is compared directly

constraints.item: Possible duty rise from 15% to 25%, decided mid-2027
constraints.effect: lowers break-even ACoS to 26.9%; made a gate before the 2028 ad budget

constraints.item: Launch timing: the plan books full-year 2027 volume although the decision is in March 2027
constraints.effect: a six-month slip in every year leaves cash near zero by 2030; the plan keeps the cross-border listing live through setup

constraints.item: Costs the pack does not give (new-SKU launch, listing takeover, Amazon storage and returns)
constraints.effect: each would erode the $2.4M cushion; stated on the cash-bridge slide

alternatives.option: Japan scale-up in 2027 (Option J), keep the cross-border Amazon test and decide on the US in 2028
alternatives.why: J fits every limit and beats A on cash to 2030 unless ACoS stays below 25.9%, but it adds $7.0M of revenue against $26.4M, in a market growing about 1.5% a year; A's downside is bounded at about $3.9M by gates

alternatives.option: National retail launch in 600 doors (Option B)
alternatives.why: breaks the cap, payback and margin floor on the planning team's own inputs, and assumes sell-through only brands above 20% awareness achieve

alternatives.option: A smaller retail test alongside Amazon in 2027
alternatives.why: the evidence cannot size a small test; it becomes the door test behind the 20% awareness gate

failure_threshold.threshold: above 28.6% (26.9% with a 25% duty) cumulative cash does not return to zero by end-2030
failure_threshold.range: cash by end-2030: low −$3.4M (32% ACoS, 25% duty) / base +$0.4M (28% pilot ACoS) / high +$2.4M (25% plan ACoS)

consistency.headline: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon as a gated launch; it fits the limits but reaches $26.4M in 2030 and pays back only below 28.6% ad cost
consistency.fix: Draft said 'only route that fits the limits'; Japan also fits, so the claim now reads 'only route that builds a sizeable US business', and payback is stated as conditional on ad cost

gap.base_case: $26.4M in 2030 on the planning team's volumes, two-thirds of the ambition

closers.option: Restate the ambition as $40M by 2032, with about $26M as the 2030 milestone

closers.size: $37.6M in 2030, still short, and breaks the cap

closers.option: Door test after the awareness gate

cases.base: pilot ACoS of 28%: cash +$0.4M by end-2030, payback just met, low point −$2.4M
cases.stress: 32% ACoS and a 25% duty: cash −$3.4M by end-2030 (payback missed), low point −$3.9M, a fifth of the cap; group margin stays above 9%

gates.response: cut broad-keyword bids, hold new SKUs
re-price or trim ad spend to keep ACoS below 26.9%
stop new spend, return to the board
test a small set of doors; otherwise stay Amazon-only
